Customer Service Officer - Freight Forwarding  
 
  Location:   Geelong, VIC    (with 1 day per fortnight in Tullamarine)   
  Salary:   $70,000 - $75,000 + Super   
  Work Type:   Full-Time, Monday to Friday (8:30 AM - 5:00 PM)  
  Industry:   Freight Forwarding & Logistics  
 
     The Opportunity     We are looking for an enthusiastic   Customer Service & Operations Officer   to join our client's team in   Geelong   on a   fixed-term contract  .  
     Key Responsibilities  
 
  Customer Support:   Act as a helpful point of contact for clients, delivering proactive updates on shipment progress.  
  Shipment Tracking:   Monitor international air and ocean freight movements (FCL/LCL).  
  Operational Admin:   Prepare customer quotations, arrange local transport, and handle invoicing/billing.  
  System Data Entry:   Accurately update shipping and customs information in   CargoWise  .  
  Team Collaboration:   Work closely with overseas agents, carriers, and offshore support teams to keep freight moving smoothly.  
 
     About You  
  Whether you have 1-2 years of experience in logistics/freight forwarding or are a sharp customer service professional looking to break into international trade, we want to hear from you!      
  What we are looking for:  
 
  Background:   1+ years in freight forwarding, transport, or customer service (exposure to air or ocean freight is a great plus!).  
  Software:   Experience with   CargoWise   is advantageous, but a willingness to learn software systems is most important.  
  Communication:   Clear, professional written and verbal communication with a positive, client-first attitude.  
  Skills:   Strong organizational skills, keen attention to detail, and ability to multi-task in a busy environment.  
  Location & Flexibility:   Based in the   Geelong   office with the ability to work from the   Tullamarine office just one day per fortnight  .  
 
  Why Apply?  
 
  Great Entry Point:   Ideal role to learn global freight forwarding operations and build a long-term logistics career.  
  Supportive Team:   Work in a close-knit, friendly environment with mentorship from experienced managers.  
  Work Near Home:   Enjoy working out of Geelong offices while staying connected to Melbourne's logistics hub.

Imagine a career filled with purpose and possibility 
 Competitive rates of pay 
 Fulfilling work that fits around your life 
 
  Employment Type:  Casual  Location:  Condobolin   About Us:  At RSL LifeCare, our Residential Care teams have the ability to make a big difference to the lives of veterans and seniors while they receive quality and compassionate care in our aged care homes. This is an opportunity for you to join a large social purpose organisation where you can have a huge positive impact and feel the personal and professional reward in return. At our core, RSL LifeCare provide care and services to veterans and seniors who live in our communities or who are receiving support at home. Our vision of creating proud communities living their best lives is at the heart of everything we do as we continue to build upon our legacy of supporting veterans and their families for more than 100 years.    About the role:  As a Catering Assistant at RSL LifeCare, every day you're empowered to make a meaningful difference to people's lives. Within our supportive work environment your compassion is valued and your professional development is prioritised. You will have the opportunity to: 
 
 Work closely with the catering team and the Head Chef to provide high quality catering services for residents and their visitors 
 Comply with Food Safety Standards 
 Maintain a clean, efficient, and professional work environment; dishwashing and cleaning the kitchen, equipment and dining areas 
 Demonstrate a customer service mindset when interacting with residents, their families and visitors 
 Serve residents meals and snacks ensuring that the correct meals are served to residents with special dietary needs 
 Build strong and productive relationships with your team to deliver a positive dining experience 
 
   Our benefits:  RSL LifeCare offers a range of benefits including: 
 
 Not-for-profit tax benefits - salary packaging of up to $31,800 per year. This allows you to reduce your taxable income by receiving part of your salary as tax-free benefits like super contributions, car leasing, and more. 
 Staff discounts across 700 select retail stores through Maxxia Rewards 
 Leave Loading - 17.5% pay top up on paid leave 
 Career opportunities across Residential Care homes and Community Services 
 
  About You:   We are excited to hear from you about this role! We are looking out for: 
 
 Your demonstrated compassion and empathy. Our teams have a passion for what they do and the impact they make to our residents and their families. 
 Your excellent communication skills, both verbal and written to ensure the best possible resident experience and teamwork 
 Your teamwork. We enjoy working together with a highly skilled team to deliver the best possible experience for our residents and support each other. 
 Your ability to work efficiently and ensure compliance with quality and safety standards 
 Qualifications in catering and hospitality or related work experience are beneficial but not essential. We can help you learn and develop in the role. 
 Australian Working Rights 
 
  Join us today and see where it takes you tomorrow!   It is a mandatory requirement for a team member working in the Aged Care sector to have a valid Police Check or a valid National Disability Insurance Scheme (NDIS) check, or potentially both, to undertake the inherent requirements of the role. Clearances must be verified prior to commencing employment with RSL LifeCare.    Our commitment to diversity:  We are proud to stand for our unique values: Do the Right Thing, Aim Higher, Care from the Heart, and Act as One team.   We welcome and encourage applications from people across our diverse community, especially from Veterans, current serving ADF personnel, their families and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander applicants. We believe everyone has the right to feel safe, respected, valued and heard regardless of their gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity or disability.  Please  click here  to apply.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Service Assistant Orderly



 Apply now
 Job no: 945367

 Work type: Full time

 Location: Eyre and Western

 Categories: Community and Social Services, Child, Aged and Disability Care, Support Services





 

Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, Port Lincoln Health Services 

Salary: WHD3 $1,250.29 to $1,281.40 per week + 12% Superannuation + Salary Sacrifice Benefits + Leave loading 

Permanent Full time position, working over a 7 day roster

Begin Your Journey as an Orderly at Eyre and Far North Local Health Network!

Port Lincoln Hospital is the region's principal healthcare facility, serving the Eyre Peninsula community with a broad range of acute and primary health services. If you take pride in practical, hands-on work and want it to genuinely matter to the people around you, this full-time ongoing role as a Service Assistant Orderly is worth your attention.

What You'll Be Doing

Working across Port Lincoln Hospital as part of the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll keep essential services moving so that clinical teams can focus on patient care. Your day-to-day responsibilities will include:

Transporting patients safely and respectfully within the hospital

Collecting, delivering, and returning equipment to the correct areas

Transporting pathology and other specimens in line with handling protocols

Managing the delivery of clean linen and timely removal of soiled linen and waste

What You'll Bring

A reliable, punctual approach and the physical capacity to perform manual handling tasks throughout a full shift

Clear, respectful communication with patients, visitors, and healthcare staff

An understanding of, or willingness to learn, infection control and safe waste-handling procedures as required within SA Health facilities

The ability to prioritise competing tasks calmly in a busy hospital environment

Why Port Lincoln Hospital

As part of SA Health and the Eyre and Far North Local Health Network, you'll have access to salary packaging benefits that can meaningfully increase your take-home pay - a genuine advantage of working in the public health sector. Port Lincoln offers an enviable lifestyle on the Eyre Peninsula, with outstanding fishing, seafood, and open coastline right on the doorstep. The hospital team is close-knit, and the work you do each day has a direct, visible impact on patients and families who rely on local care. Ongoing employment means genuine job security, with the support and structure of one of South Australia's largest health employers behind you.

Ready to Apply?

Submit your application through the SA Health careers portal. Include a current resume and a brief cover letter outlining your suitability for the role. For questions about the position, reach out to the hiring manager - their details are listed in the role profile.

About Us 

With its ancient outback landscapes, boutique vineyards, oyster farms and Australia's best-kept-secret surf coast, Eyre and Far North will inspire and energise you.

Our capabilities span across Telecommunications, Finance, Insurance, health, Public Services, Print / Digital Media, Broadcast and Supply Chain. Dipole Group is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

Position Overview
We are seeking an experienced Backup & Storage Administrator to join our Managed Services team supporting mission-critical telecommunications infrastructure and enterprise platforms. The successful candidate will be responsible for the administration, monitoring, maintenance, optimization, and lifecycle management of enterprise backup and storage environments, ensuring high availability, performance, data protection, business continuity, and disaster recovery in accordance with agreed Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

Key Responsibilities: 

Storage Administration: 
Administer and support enterprise storage environments across Production, UAT, Development, Test, and Disaster Recovery environments.
Manage SAN, NAS, Fibre Channel, iSCSI, and enterprise storage infrastructure.
Perform storage provisioning, LUN allocation, zoning, masking, expansion, and capacity management.
Monitor storage health, performance, utilization, and availability using enterprise monitoring tools.
Perform storage performance tuning and optimization.
Support storage replication, snapshots, cloning, and disaster recovery solutions.
Perform firmware upgrades, storage migrations, lifecycle management, and maintenance activities.
Troubleshoot and resolve storage-related incidents within agreed SLA and KPI targets.
Conduct Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and implement preventive measures.

Backup Administration:
Administer and support enterprise backup infrastructure.
Configure and manage backup policies, schedules, retention policies, and media management.
Monitor backup jobs and ensure successful completion of backup and restore operations.
Perform backup recovery testing and validation.
Manage backup replication between Production and Disaster Recovery environments.
Perform backup infrastructure upgrades, patching, and maintenance.
Support disaster recovery exercises and business continuity testing.
Troubleshoot failed backup jobs and optimize backup performance.
Ensure backup compliance with security, governance, and retention requirements.

Operational Support:
Collaborate with Database, VMware, Linux, Windows, Network, Security, and Application Support teams.
Participate in Incident, Problem, Change, Release, and Capacity Management processes following ITIL best practices.
Develop operational documentation, runbooks, knowledge articles, and standard operating procedures.
Ensure compliance with operational procedures, security standards, and governance requirements.
Identify automation opportunities and implement continuous service improvements.
Participate in planned maintenance activities and 24x7 on-call support rotations.

Required Experience:

Experience working within Managed Services or Enterprise Infrastructure Operations.
Experience supporting large-scale enterprise backup and storage environments.
Experience working in mission-critical production environments with strict SLA and KPI commitments.
Experience supporting Telecommunications, Service Providers, or large enterprise environments is highly desirable.
Experience working in 24x7 operational support environments.

Full-time Passive Fire Protection Equipment Technician position available with competitive salary. Work in a dynamic team in NSW.

3 Stand-out Bullet Points:
•	Full-Time Fire Protection Equipment Technician
•	Salary Range: $90,000 - $105,000 per annum plus superannuation
•	Exciting opportunity to work in a professional setting.

About Us
Essential Passive Fire Protection Services Pty Ltd is a proudly Australian-owned and operated company dedicated to delivering premier facility maintenance and safety solutions. We specialise in comprehensive fire protection services, ensuring that commercial, industrial, and residential properties remain safe, compliant, and fully operational. Our commitment to excellence, regulatory compliance, and workplace safety forms the foundation of our operations, enabling us to provide unparalleled service to our diverse client base.

About the role
The Passive Fire Protection Equipment Technician is responsible for ensuring that all passive fire containment systems are correctly installed, inspected, tested, and maintained in strict compliance with the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and applicable Australian Standards, primarily AS 1851. The role involves working with a variety of passive fire systems, including but not limited to fire-rated batts, wraps, mastic, collars, seals, fire doors, smoke doors, and fire shutters.

Duties and Responsibilities

•	Install, repair, and maintain passive fire containment systems, including fire-rated batts, wraps, mastic, collars, seals, fire/smoke doors, and shutters.
•	Ensure all installations and maintenance works are executed in accordance with manufacturer specifications, the BCA, and relevant Australian Standards.
•	Select and apply appropriate fire-stopping materials for various penetrations and construction joints.
•	Conduct routine inspections and preventative maintenance testing of passive fire protection systems in accordance with AS 1851.
•	Assess the integrity of fire compartments, fire doors, smoke doors, and fire shutters.
•	Identify, diagnose, and report on defects, non-conformances, or compromised fire separations.
•	Perform necessary rectification and repair works on non-compliant passive fire systems to restore full regulatory compliance.
•	Provide technical recommendations for the upgrade or replacement of obsolete or irreparably damaged passive fire infrastructure.
•	Accurately complete and submit service reports, logbooks, defect notices, and compliance certificates in a timely manner.
•	Maintain comprehensive digital and physical records of all inspections, tests, and rectification works using the company’s designated field service management software.
•	Capture and upload clear photographic evidence of pre- and post-rectification works.
•	Ensure the correct use, maintenance, and storage of all Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), tools, and company vehicles.

Essential Skills

•	Comprehensive understanding of the Building Code of Australia (BCA) and AS 1851 as they relate to passive fire protection.
•	Ability to read, interpret, and work from architectural drawings, engineering plans, and fire matrix schedules.
•	High level of attention to detail and precision in workmanship.
•	Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to troubleshoot complex compliance issues on-site.
•	Proficiency in using mobile technology (tablets/smartphones) and field service management software for reporting and documentation.
•	Excellent time management skills with the capacity to work autonomously and manage a daily schedule of site visits.
•	Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Qualifications needed:

•	Minimum Certificate III level or equivalent relevant work experience
•	Minimum one year of work experience on relevant position
•	White card

What We Offer

•	Competitive salary based on experience
•	Opportunities for professional growth and training
•	A supportive and dynamic work environment
•	Work on exciting projects with cutting-edge technology

Salary:  The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $90,000-$105,000 plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

How to Apply: 11 Recruitment is your pathway to securing this exciting opportunity. We are looking forward to facilitating your application and potentially welcoming you to a company that values expertise. Apply now and let us help you take the next step in your career.

About Us

Driven by our “Safety | Service | Production” principles and over 17 years of operations excellence. Core Drilling Services has positioned itself as a leading boutique full-service provider that is agile and adaptive to the various requirements of our clients.

We specialize in innovative semi-autonomous and conventional drill rig packages, offering expert technical services in reverse circulation, diamond, geological and geotechnical sampling services Australia-wide.

About the Role

The Driller plays a key role in overseeing and operating drilling equipment, ensuring safety, efficiency, and productivity while managing the crew, maintaining equipment, and adhering to safety and environmental regulations.

Some of the responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

* Lead drill rig and site moves, ensuring optimal positioning for efficiency and safety.
* Operate and maintain drill rig systems and equipment efficiently.
* Set up and dismantle drilling equipment and machinery, ensuring readiness for operation.
* Perform routine and scheduled maintenance to minimize downtime, including greasing, checking fluid levels, and cleaning the rig.
* Report any mechanical defects or anomalies to the Drill Rig Supervisor.
* Take responsibility for the health, safety, and performance of the drill crew.
* Ensure compliance with safety regulations, including correct PPE use and maintaining a clean, safe work environment.
* Identify and address hazards or risks during daily operations.
* Refuel and restock the drill rig for the next crew at handover.
* Schedule and complete maintenance in line with the drilling cycle or shift change to maximize efficiency.
* Monitor drilling parameters (pressure, depth, weight, etc.) to ensure smooth operation.
* Record operational data, including drilling depth, rate of penetration, and any anomalies.
* Complete and submit consumable orders each weekend before COB Sunday.
* Accurately complete and submit all required documentation, including daily PLODs.
* Manage the drill rig budget effectively.
* Identify and report initiatives to improve safety, productivity, and efficiency.
* Maintain and update all compliance registers for the drill rig.
* Support the development and implementation of organizational procedures and processes.
* Maintain a high standard of housekeeping around the drill pad and work areas at all times.
* Maintain focus on time utilization and operational efficiency.
* Mentor and guide drill crew members to ensure safe and efficient operations.

Qualifications and Criteria

* Relevant trade qualifications (Certificate III or IV in Drilling Operations) – desirable
* Minimum of 2 years relevant experience working in a similar role - preferred
* Valid Manual Driver’s Licence (HR class)
* National Police Check (issued within the last 12 months)
* Current CPR Certificate (issued within the last 12 months)
* Current First Aid Certificate (issued within the last 2 years)
* 4WD Group 1 Certificate (issued within the last 2 years)
* Fire Extinguisher Training Certificate (issued within the last 2 years) – preferred
* Working Safely at Heights Certificate (issued within the last 2 years) – preferred
* Strong mechanical aptitude
* Proven ability to follow instructions and adhere to safety procedures
* Demonstrated strong work ethic and ability to work effectively in a team
* Good problem-solving skills
* Effective verbal and written communication skills

Salary range: $90,000 – $130,000 per annum (depending on experience and qualifications)

At Core Drilling Services, you’ll be part of a company that values teamwork, innovation, and personal growth. We offer long-term opportunities for professional development, a supportive team culture, and the chance to work with advanced drilling technology.

About Us
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory and beyond.

About the Employer
We are supporting an automotive business (ABN 69 669 060 913) based in Acacia Ridge, Queensland, specialising in Japanese vehicle imports, compliance, mechanical repairs, servicing, and vehicle inspections. With over 20 years of industry experience and a commitment to quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. The business is seeking a Motor Mechanic to support its growing operations and to maintain, test, diagnose and repair petrol engines and the mechanical components of lightweight motor vehicles, including transmissions, suspension, steering and braking systems.

Salary: $79,423 to $83,000 per annum plus superannuation
Location: Acacia Ridge, QLD
Employment Type: Full-time, ongoing
Ordinary Hours: 38 hours per week

Key Responsibilities
- Detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults in petrol engines and vehicle components.
- Use automotive diagnostic scan tools, computers, multimeters, pressure gauges and other testing equipment to identify faults.
- Inspect and test petrol engines, transmissions, steering systems, suspension systems, brakes and related mechanical components.
- Dismantle and remove engine assemblies, transmissions, steering mechanisms and other mechanical components.
- Examine dismantled parts and components for wear, damage, defects and serviceability.
- Repair or replace worn, damaged and defective mechanical parts.
- Reassemble petrol engines and mechanical components following repairs.
- Test and adjust repaired mechanical components to confirm correct operation and performance.
- Perform scheduled maintenance services, including oil and filter changes, lubrication, fluid replacement and engine tune-ups.
- Diagnose and repair fuel, ignition, cooling and engine-management systems.
- Service and repair transmissions, steering, suspension and braking systems.
- Complete vehicle road tests and post-repair inspections.
- Confirm that repairs have been completed correctly and that vehicles operate safely.
- Follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals, technical bulletins and workshop procedures.
- Inspect vehicles for roadworthiness and identify repairs required to meet applicable roadworthiness standards.
- Issue roadworthiness or safety certificates where appropriately licensed or authorised.
- Respond to vehicle breakdown service calls where required.
- Accurately record diagnostic findings, repairs completed, parts used and further work recommended.
- Complete job cards, service records and workshop documentation.
- Safely operate vehicle hoists, mechanical tools, power tools and diagnostic equipment.
- Maintain a clean, safe and organised workshop.
- Comply with workplace health and safety and environmental requirements.
- Assist apprentices or junior workshop employees where reasonably required.

Selection Criteria
1. Light-vehicle mechanical expertise
Demonstrated experience maintaining and repairing petrol-powered passenger and light commercial vehicles.
2. Diagnostic skills
Ability to detect and diagnose mechanical and related electrical faults using automotive diagnostic equipment.
3. Mechanical repair skills
Experience repairing petrol engines, transmissions, brakes, steering and suspension systems.
4. Technical knowledge
Ability to understand and follow manufacturer specifications, service manuals and technical repair information.
5. Problem-solving ability
Ability to identify vehicle faults, determine suitable repair methods and resolve mechanical problems efficiently.
6. Quality workmanship
Strong attention to detail and commitment to completing repairs to an appropriate trade and safety standard.
7. Organisation
Ability to manage allocated workshop jobs, maintain accurate records and complete repairs within required timeframes.
8. Communication and teamwork
Ability to communicate repair findings clearly and work effectively with workshop staff, management and service personnel.
9. Safety awareness
Demonstrated understanding of workshop safety, safe equipment operation and environmentally responsible waste disposal.

Required Qualifications and Experience
- AQF Certificate III in Light Vehicle Mechanical Technology, AQF Certificate IV, or an equivalent recognised automotive mechanical qualification.
- Relevant practical experience servicing and repairing petrol-powered lightweight motor vehicles.
- At least three years of relevant experience
- Experience using automotive diagnostic scan tools and testing equipment.
- Experience diagnosing and repairing petrol engines and associated mechanical systems.
- Current driver licence.
- Ability to work full-time in Brisbane.

How to Apply
We are looking for a reliable, skilled, and safety-minded automotive professional to support vehicle servicing, repairs, inspections, and workshop operations while maintaining high standards of quality, efficiency, and customer service.

To apply, please submit the following:
- Resume outlining your work experience and references.
- A short cover letter of no more than 300 words explaining:
- Why you are applying for this position; and
- An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork. Please use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result.
- A written response of no more than 600 words describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role. Please structure your example or examples using the STAR method.

* Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a professional and growing automotive business that values quality, safety, teamwork, reliability, and customer satisfaction, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Phone calls and walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Applications Close: 13 August 2026
